insights.text: The model reads heat patterns well in unseen cities: R² 0.74 (offset removed), Spearman 0.86, AUC 0.93, no city below the city-mean baseline.
The final model cut unexplained variance by 43 % and raised hotspot F1 by 20 % over the first model; the anomaly target alone did not (smaller anomaly model R² 0.53, F1 0.47).
The three cities that failed under the first model are now in the top half: Bengaluru 0.09→0.76, Bhubaneswar 0.12→0.73, Kolkata 0.14→0.79.
Hot pixels are underestimated by 1.35 °C on average, much of it Dehradun (-3.99 °C); without Dehradun the mean is -1.05 °C.
City quality varies: Amritsar is best (MAE 0.54, AUC 0.97, F1 0.76), Lucknow weakest on pattern (R² 0.64, Spearman 0.74); Dehradun and Coimbatore have high MAE but good ranking.
On the hottest 600 m blocks the model sees only about half the observed excess (Jaipur 2.2 of 4.4 °C, Delhi 2.0 of 4.5 °C), so doses close only the explainable part.
Vegetation dominates: shuffling it drops R² by 0.89; planting 45 % beats cool roofs on 99 % in the Delhi block; the model's NDVI effect is 11 to 25 % steeper than the data's.
insights._source: metrics.json group_importance, vegetation_check; cooling.json rows[1]; README.md:135-141

inconsistencies.text: 'R² inside the city' 0.74 in README hero/headline is the offset-removed metric; the per-city 'R² inside' column averages 0.72.
The hot_AUC rows average 0.936 (rounds to 0.94), but the README mean is 0.93; within rounding tolerance.
README says 2.4 °C is not explained for the Delhi block; the table gives 4.5 - 2.0 = 2.5 °C.
Delhi area dose pools (190 ha greenable + 158 ha built) exceed the 211 ha area, so the pools likely overlap; uncertain.
The land-cover pixel total (17.81 M) is about all pixels of 10 cities (89 M / 50 × 10), despite 'usable pixels' masking; uncertain.
Delhi (hotspot quality, cooling, drivers) is a training city per the default split; only Jaipur is held out.
